messages:
mike: quick PSA — after the kernel-selection roll (kernel-v3 -> kernel-v4) we saw a pronounced tail divergence for long-sequence tenants. small repro attached in thread.
anya: ugh, saw alerts too. long-running tenant queues ballooned, short seqs stayed fine. suspect batch formation + kernel choice interaction.
devon: timeline? which deploy + which perf reg? any flamegraphs?
mike: deploy @ 2156740000, rollout 20%. perf-bot posted a short summary: `p50 ~ unchanged, p95 +18%, p99 +43% for sequences >1024`.
perf-bot: regression summary: kernel-v4 changes: different matmul tile, changed KV-prefetch ordering. Profiling shows CPU thread stalls during KV cache lookup for long sequences.
sam: can you paste the perf snippet? small CL maybe enough to revert if obvious.
mike: logs:
```
[batcher] formed 16 mini-batches -> 4 long-only batches
[kv] miss-rate 0.12 -> 0.46 (for tenant=acme-corp)
[kernel] chosen: kernel-v4 (latency-opt) but degrades on long KV-warm paths
```
anya: interesting that miss-rate jumps only for some tenants — maybe tenant-specific sequence distributions expose eviction thrash.
devon: hypothesis: continuous-batcher groups by arrival window; kernel-v4 expects denser KV hits and benefits from larger minibatches, but for tenant mix with sporadic long prefixes we get more cache churn and larger token budgets consumed by long seqs -> short seqs get starved indirectly.
ops-bot: FYI: another symptom — reclaim loop hits higher CPU, which caused scheduling delays on the batch-worker pod.
mike: proposed experiment plan:
1) pin kernel selection to kernel-v3 for tenants with >15% long sequences (quick rollback path)
2) tweak batcher queue-policy: cap mini-batch size for long sequences to avoid one long-request soaking token budget
3) run a rebalancer that gives short sequences a soft token credit refill every N batches
4) run candidate for 6h with perf sampling and flamegraphs
anya: can we do (2) as a config flag first? i.e. batcher.long_seq_max_mini=8 instead of changing global behavior
devon: yes, we can gate it behind `batcher.experimental.long_seq_cap=true` and A/B by tenant tag.
sam: add a quick telemetry counter: `batcher.evicted_tokens_by_tenant` and `kv.miss_rate_by_tenant` — want to correlate.
mike: I'll open a small PR with the flag + revert rule. PR: <https://git.company/infra/PR/4321>
perf-bot: experiment results (after 3h): p99 long tenants down -27%, overall throughput stable, kv.miss_rate improved from 0.46 -> 0.26 for affected tenants.
anya: nice. any regression for short seqs?
perf-bot: short seq p50 unchanged, p95 improved -4% in canary tenants. token-credit refill looks promising.
devon: next steps: run 24h sweep and confirm no cache blowout. Also run kernel head-to-head with the batcher flag on to see if kernel-v4 still beneficial in mixed loads.
mike: also want to add a mini-slab policy: preserve a small per-tenant KV pool for long seqs to reduce eviction oscillation. low-risk config first.
sam: remind me — do we have per-tenant KV quota metric surfaced in console? if not, let's add it to the rollout dashboard.
ops-bot: created dashboard ticket: OPS-2134
mike: thanks — I'll coordinate rollout plan and update PR. output a short postmortem if 24h sweep looks good.
anya: leave the kernel pinned until we have the head-to-head with config on. :thumbsup:
devon: noted. I'll run perf harness overnight and post flamegraphs.
mike: leaving notes here so infra/ops and experiments aren't blind. will update thread with links to graphs + final numbers.
perf-bot: experiment artifacts uploaded: <https://storage.company/experiments/2156789012/artifacts.zip>
